small_guidance:
- The GEMM kernel sets `allow_tf32=False`, which on a 4090 (Ada) forces full FP32 mma and roughly halves tensor-core throughput. Switch to `tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=True)` — this is the single biggest win available without redesign.
- Add larger-K configs to the autotune list (e.g. `BLOCK_K=64/128` with `num_stages=4`) since K=8192 is large; also add a `BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=4` config. Drop the masked K-tail loads by issuing a clean inner loop (K is a multiple of 64) so the hot loop has no per-iter mask compute.
- In `group_norm_hardtanh_kernel`, CPG = 8192/16 = 512. Use `BLOCK=512` exactly (power of two already), `num_warps=8`, `num_stages=2`, and load `x` once into registers reused for both reduction passes (already done) — also load `w`,`b` with `mask=mask` removed since CPG is a clean power of two; emit unmasked loads to cut predicate overhead.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite the GEMM to use TF32 tensor cores (the dominant cost: 1024×8192×8192 ≈ 137 GFLOP per call). With `allow_tf32=True` and proper pipelining (num_stages=4, BLOCK_K=64), the 4090 should hit several TFLOPs and bring GEMM well under 1 ms; current 4.48 ms is consistent with FP32-mma throughput.
- Consider fusing the GroupNorm's first-pass reduction into the GEMM epilogue: each `(M, BLOCK_N)` tile already has the post-bias activations in registers; if `BLOCK_N` aligns to a group's channel count (CPG=512), accumulate per-group partial sums and sum-of-squares into a workspace, then a tiny second kernel finalizes mean/rstd and applies affine+hardtanh. This removes a full read/write pass of the 1024×8192 intermediate.
- Alternatively, persist the GEMM output in a `channels_last`-friendly layout (already row-major here) and launch the GN kernel with one program per row covering all 16 groups in a single block (BLOCK=8192, num_warps=16) so the row stays in L2/SMEM across both passes; this would cut launch and L2-traffic overhead on the norm step.
